title: Laredo City Council Meets Today: $584,500 International Boulevard Deal, Scooter Rules on the Table
excerpt: The Laredo City Council meets today, Monday, Nov. 16, with a $584,500 road deal on the agenda — a reconstruction agreement for a section of International Boulevard that the city and a private freight company would pay for together.
content:
The Laredo City Council meets today, Monday, Nov. 16, with a $584,500 road deal on the agenda — a reconstruction agreement for a section of International Boulevard that the city and a private freight company would pay for together.

Under the agreement with International Freight Forwarding, Inc., the two sides would put $584,546 into escrow to start: the city would contribute $450,000, about 77 percent, and the company would contribute $134,546, about 23 percent. The money would cover design, construction and related costs.

The city holds an easement on land owned by the company along that stretch of International Boulevard, and because of that easement the city bears responsibility for maintaining the road. The existing asphalt pavement has had persistent maintenance problems, and the city originally planned to rebuild it with asphalt again. The company proposed upgrading to concrete pavement instead, arguing it would last longer and need less maintenance — and both sides signed a construction agreement reflecting the change.

The council is being asked to ratify that agreement, which both parties have already signed. The proposal also sets out who pays for the cost difference created by the concrete upgrade.

According to KGNS, the council is also scheduled to discuss department service reports, a border project and scooter rules at today's meeting. Webb Watch 956 will report what the council decides.
